artworks.title: The House that Jeff Built
artworks.medium: etching in black on wove paper
artworks.description: Printed with black ink on off-white paper, twelve scenes are laid out in a grid of three rows and four columns. The sheet is titled “THE HOUSE THAT JEFF BUILT,” and most scenes show Black and white people or tools used in enforcing slavery. Each entry also has text below. They appear as follows. At the top left, the first image is of a wooden door in a wooden building with a barred window. Writing over the door lintel reads, “SLAVE PEN” and a sheet hung to the left of the door reads, “SLAVE SALE, AUCTION, Prime Lot, COTTON.” Text below the image reads, “This is the House that Jeff built.” The next scene is of three tied bales in front of the wooden wall of the house. The poster is visible on the wall, and text below reads, “This is the cotton by rebels call’d king, (Tho’ call’d by loyalists no such thing), That lay in the house that Jeff built.” Next are three Black adults and one Black child harvesting cotton. One adult holds a sack open and another carries a sack slung over one shoulder while the child picks the cotton. Text below reads, “These are field-chattels that made cotton kin, (Tho’ call’d by loyalists no such thing,) That lay in the house that Jeff built.” The final image on the top line shows two Black men sitting on a bench and two women and two children standing in front of the sale poster. Text below reads, “These are the chattels, babes, mothers, and men, To be sold by the head, in the slave pen: A part of the house that Jeff built.” Next is a white man wearing a suit and holding a gavel while standing behind a podium. The poster is laid on the surface in front of him, and text below reads, “This is the thing by some call’d a man, Whose trade is to sell all the chattels he can, From yearlings to adults of life’s longest span: In and out of the house that Jeff built.” The next illustration shows a ball and chain with an open padlock at the base of a post with shackles hanging from a nail. Text reads, “These are the shackles, for slaves who suppose, Their limbs are their own from fingers to toes; And are prone to believe say all that can, That they shouldn’t be sold by that thing call’d a man: Whose trade is to sell all the chattels he can, From yearlings to adults of life’s longest span: In and out of the house that Jeff built.” Next, four white men stand in line and one has a hand on the upper arm of a Black woman. Three of the men wear top hats and suits, and the fourth has a bulging belly, a floppy hat, and a slip of paper hanging from his jacket pocket. “These buy the slaves both make and female, And sell their own souls to a boss with a tail, Who owns the small soul of that thing call’d a man, Whose trade is to sell all the chattels he can, From yearlings to adults of life’s longest span: In and out of the house that Jeff built.” Next, two white man wear suits and stand next to a table in front of a portrait labeled J. Davis and Gen. Beauregard. One standing man gestures at a Black man who stands to one side. “Here the slave breeder parts with his own flesh, To a trader down south, in the heart of secesh., Thus trader and breeder secure without fail, The lasting attachment of him with a tail, Who owns the small soul of that thing call’d a man, Whose trade is to sell all the chattels he can, From yearlings to adults of life’s longest span, In and out of the house that Jeff built.” The final row begins with a whip and the text, “This is the scourge by some call’d the cat, Stout in the handle, and nine tails to that: Tis joyous to think that the time’s drawing near, When the cat will no longer cause chattels to fear, Nor the going, going, gone of that thing call’d a man, Whose trade is to sell all the chattels he can, From yearlings to adults of life’s longest span, In and out of the house that Jeff built.” Next, a bare-chested black woman is tied to a post and a white man holds out a cat-o-nine-tails. Her back is sliced with gashes. “Here the slave driver in transport applies, Nine tails to his victim, nor heeds her shrill cries. Alas! that a driver with nine tails his own; Should be a slave to a driver who owns only one: Albeit he owns that thing call’d a man, Whose trade is to sell all the chattels he can, From yearlings to adults of lifes longest span, In and out of the house that Jeff built.” Next is the head and shoulders of a white man who looks down and to our left under gathered, thunderous brows. He has a beaked nose, a long upper lip, downturned lips, and hollow cheekbones. “Here’s the arch rebel Jeff whose infamous course, Has bro’t rest to the plow, and made active the hearse, And invoked on his head every patriots curse, Spread ruin, and famine, to stock the slave pen, And furnish employment to that thing among men, Whose trade is to sell all the chattels he can, From yearlings to adults of life’s longest span: In and out of the house that Jeff built.” The final image is of the iron ball among broken shackles, chains, a broken gavel, and torn up sale posters. One intact poster reads, “Execution of JEFF DAVIS the TRAITOR, Dying speech and CONFESSION” under an image of a person hanging from a gallows. Text reads, “But Jeff’s infamous house, is doom’d to come down. So says uncle Sam, and so said John Brown. With slave pen, and auction, shackles, driver, and cat, Together with seller, and buyer, and breeder, and that, Most loathsome of bipeds by some call’d a man, Whose trade is to sell all the chattels he can, From yearlings to adults of lifes longest span, In and out of the house that Jeff built.”

artworks.title: Ah! Fouchtrra! ... Ma femme ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures in conversation in a setting with wooden barrels and a basket. One figure is a man in ragged clothing with a cap, standing near a woman wearing a full-length dress and a bonnet. The background includes a stack of wooden barrels and a basket. The style is reminiscent of Honoré Daumier, known for caricatures and social commentaries. The lines and shadows in the drawing convey a sense of movement and texture.

artworks.title: Viaduct, Coal Pockets
artworks.medium: etching in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of Frank B. Bristow, 1968)
artworks.description: The image portrays an urban scene seen from an elevated perspective. A large arch bridge is dominant in the background, with figures walking across it. To the right are tall buildings with intricate line details and a textured surface. In the foreground, there is a construction site with wood and mechanical equipment. The color palette is sepia toned, accentuating details and creating a historical atmosphere. Urban buildings and scaffolding can be seen in the distance.

artworks.title: Little Mereton Hall, Cheshire
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.description: This is a painting of a manor with a courtyard scene of festivity. The building is designed in Tudor style with timber-framed construction and leaded glass windows. In the courtyard, people are dancing in vibrant attire, with rich reds, blues, and yellows. The building has intricate architectural details like carved wooden gables and decorative motifs. Greenery climbs some structures, adding to the liveliness of the scene. The sky has soft clouds, creating a gentle ambiance. The painting is in the style of 19th-century reproductive prints focused on cultural landmarks and scenes.

artworks.title: The Hurdy-Gurdy Boy
artworks.medium: lithograph in black with tan stone tint on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Alice F. Williams, 1958)
artworks.description: The image shows a young boy seated with a musical instrument, likely a hurdy-gurdy, in his lap. He gazes off to the side with a relaxed expression. The boy wears a jacket with visible buttons and a white shirt collar. The background includes a textured wall and bare branches with a few leaves.

artworks.title: Harvard College Bookplate with the Christo et Ecclesiæ Seal
artworks.medium: engraving in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Alice Farley Williams, 1962)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an ornate bookplate. The design features a heraldic shield with an inscription in Latin around it. Above the shield, there are stacks of books with a radiant sun with a face. On either side of the shield, there are intricate floral and scroll patterns with small globes positioned on pedestals. Below the shield, there is a draped banner with the word "Thorndike" and the year "1818." At the bottom, the artist's name, "N. Hurd Sc." and the location "BOSTON" are inscribed. The design is detailed and symmetrical.

artworks.title: Harvard College Bookplate with the Christo et Ecclesiæ Seal
artworks.medium: engraving in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Alice Farley Williams, 1962)
artworks.description: This is an image of a coat of arms or emblem with ornamental designs. It includes a central shield with a chevron and open books, surrounded by intricate floral and scroll designs. Above the shield is a radiant sun with a human face, resting on stacked books. Below are decorative curtain-like elements hanging from stylized columns with globes on top. The composition is symmetrical and the style resembles traditional European heraldry.

artworks.title: Fidèles aux vieux usages ...
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an interior scene with three individuals engaged in different activities. The room is adorned with a large framed picture on the wall. On the left, a seated individual with a scarf around their neck is observing. They sit on a simple wooden chair. In the middle, a person is adjusting their collar. On the far right, another person is using a towel, possibly drying their hands or preparing for a task. The style is reminiscent of 19th-century European illustration, depicting everyday life with a focus on domestic activities. The detailed line work and shading add texture and depth to the scene, reflecting social or cultural practices of the era.

artworks.title: Gertrude Climbed a Widowed Father's Knee
artworks.artist: Ferdinand Joubert, after George Elgar Hicks
artworks.medium: engraving in black on wove paper
artworks.description: The image depicts a man sitting on a chair with a child sitting on his lap. The man has one arm resting on a large chest next to him and the other arm around the child. The man's facial features are subtle in a line drawing style, with his eyes looking downward and one hand partially covering his face. He has short, slightly wavy hair and is dressed in a period-style suit. The child, with long hair, wears a simple dress and is embracing the man. The background shows minimal details of paneled walls and a bed, suggesting a room interior. The illustration is a simple line drawing.

artworks.title: The Little Nurseling, Take Him to Thy Love
artworks.artist: Ferdinand Joubert, after George Elgar Hicks
artworks.medium: engraving in black on wove paper
artworks.description: The image depicts four figures in a drawing. In the center, there is a Native American man standing upright, holding a long spear in one hand and resting his other hand on the head of a child next to him. He is wearing traditional attire, including a feathered headdress and a cloth draped over his shoulder. Beside him, on the left, is a man in colonial-style clothing, bending slightly forward with one arm extended towards the Native American man. Kneeling beside the colonial man is a young girl holding onto his leg, dressed in a long, modest dress. Another child stands to the right of the Native American man, looking downwards. The background features a simple, pastoral setting with lines indicating trees or foliage, a wooden structure on the right, and a picket fence that recedes into the distance.

artworks.title: A Form Has Rushed amidst Them from the Dark
artworks.artist: Ferdinand Joubert, after George Elgar Hicks
artworks.medium: engraving in black on wove paper
artworks.description: The image depicts four figures in a room. On the left, a man stands with one foot forward, holding a long weapon or stick, wearing 19th-century clothing. Beside him, a bald man is holding onto a woman. The woman has long hair and is dressed in a long dress. On the right, another man with a plumed headdress holds a shield and a bow. The room has wood slat walls, a table with pitchers and a cup, and a hanging item, with a suggestion of an open door or window on the right.

artworks.title: Le Cafe
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of Frank B. Bristow, 1968)
artworks.description: The image depicts a sketched scene of a social gathering in a café or bar setting. The scene includes several partially visible figures, focusing on the upper bodies and heads of individuals. In the foreground, a woman in a striped dress and hat is talking to a man seated at a table. The man has distinct facial features and wears a top hat. Additional men are seated around the table, some wearing hats, and a woman is also present. Bottles and glasses are on the table. In the background, there are indistinct lines representing a vertical structure, potentially windows or decor. The sketch is done with loose, expressive lines, suggesting movement and a lively atmosphere in the bustling environment.

artworks.title: Les facconnant les Moldo-Valaques ...
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a character manipulating a group of figures. The dominant figure has exaggerated features, such as a large mustache and is wearing traditional or theatrical Russian attire, possibly influencing or directing a line of figures. The figures are crawling or kneeling on the ground. The dominant figure is holding a pipe, with smoke curling into the air, and is pointing with a stick or baton to direct the subjugated figures. The figures in line wear hats. The style is typical of political or satirical illustrations, using caricature and exaggerated expressions to convey a narrative or critique.

artworks.title: Old Houses at Stroudwater
artworks.medium: etching in black on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mr. S.R. Koehler, Boston, Massachusetts, 1881)
artworks.description: The image shows a rural landscape with trees and rustic buildings. The view is from a slightly elevated angle, with the horizon high in the image and tall trees marking the boundary against the sky. The etching technique creates intricate lines for the trees, buildings, and foliage. The color scheme is black and white. A figure walks on a path, and wooden houses are seen in the distance, partially hidden by vegetation. Linear cloud formations decorate the sky.

artworks.title: Banks of the Yanne (Les Bord de la Yanne)
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of E. Gerald Lamboley, 1993)
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape viewed from a slightly elevated vantage point. The horizon is visible near the top of the image, emphasizing the vastness of the terrain. The sky and land blend seamlessly at the horizon, with no distinct structures in sight. Delicate cross-hatching is used to create shades and textures, with a monochromatic color palette of soft greys and whites. Sparse bushes are depicted in the foreground, with denser vegetation further away, leading to the open landscape in the distance. The linework captures the natural textures of the earth and greenery, resulting in a serene and detailed scene.

artworks.title: Ayant enfin trouvé le moyen d'utiliser leurs loisirs!
artworks.description: Three men are sitting together in the image. Two men wear turbans while the man in the middle wears a military hat. The man on the left has a mustache and a beard, wearing loose-fitting clothes. The man in the middle wears a military uniform. The man on the right has a mustache and goatee, wearing a turban and loose-fitting tunic. All three men are holding large spindles. The background shows a large column and indistinct figures around them.

artworks.title: Dire que peut-être j'en serai réduit ...
artworks.description: The image depicts a person standing in profile wearing a military-style uniform. The person has a prominent mustache, neatly styled hair, and is holding a top hat while a sword is slung at their side. The background is sketched with minimal detail, suggesting an indoor setting with a column or draped area to the right of the person.

artworks.title: Gopsmor Cottage
artworks.description: The image shows a highly detailed, densely hatched artwork portraying several people in motion. The figures are caught mid-action in a crowded setting. The individuals appear to be in a scene full of dynamic movement, possibly in a gathering or busy event space. The facial features and hair of the people are obscured by shadows and intricate cross-hatching. The people seem to be wearing dark clothing, suggested by the darker tones in the image. The background is composed of dense cross-hatching, with intersecting lines suggesting an indoor environment with possible overhead beams or structures, contributing to the overall sense of movement and energy.

artworks.title: Qui veut de la couronne de Bysance?
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring exaggerated characters. There are two central figures: one wears a plume-topped hat and ragged clothes with a comically contorted expression, while the other wears a crown and regal attire, holding out a crown towards the former. In the background, two additional figures dressed in a similar exaggerated fashion are in motion. The style is characterized by strong lines and exaggerated features, giving it a satirical tone. The expressions and poses of the characters amplify the comic intent of the piece. Text above and below the image suggests it is a commentary or caricature on a specific theme or event.

artworks.title: Saint Serge ... Mon bon Saint Serge!
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a person interacting with a ghostly figure. There is a spectral figure with a halo, called "Saint Serge," alongside another figure gesturing dramatically towards it. The ghostly figure is elongated and ethereal, with flowing drapery resembling a robe. The second figure appears to be dressed in a theatrical or period costume, posed in a way that suggests communication with the spectral figure. The style shows strong contrasts of light and shadow, typical of caricatures, emphasizing exaggerated features and expressions. The background is minimally detailed, focusing attention on the interaction between the two figures.

artworks.title: Le czar a Sébastopol
artworks.description: The image shows a caricature of two people with exaggerated features. The person in the foreground is leaning forward with their arms resting on a ledge, wearing a grand military uniform with epaulets and a hat. The person behind them stands straight with their arms at their sides, and is also dressed in a military uniform. Both are depicted in a black-and-white sketch style. In the background, there is a distant view of a city with buildings and flags on hills, as well as flowing water suggestive of a waterfront setting.

artworks.title: Le séduira-t-il? Les Paris sont ouverts
artworks.description: The image displays two figures from head to toe. The person on the left has dark hair tied back, wearing a dress and crown, standing with a hand on the hip. The figure on the right is taller, wearing a crown, cape, and boots, leaning towards the first person and holding their hand. In the background, two groups of soldiers face each other with rifles and bayonets. The setting seems to be a public place or arena with onlookers.

artworks.title: David Playing before Saul
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows multiple figures in various poses. The central figure is a man with an athletic build, shown in full body. He is slightly turned to the side, looking over his shoulder towards the group behind him. He has short, curly dark hair and is wearing a short, striped cloth wrapped around his waist. He carries a quiver of arrows slung over his shoulder and a bow in his other hand. Surrounding him are several other individuals; an older man with long hair and a beard raising his arm, a seated woman in a flowing dress with a prominent belt, and several other figures in the background, some wearing armor and helmets. The environment is reminiscent of a grand, ancient setting, possibly a hall with large arches and columns. The foreground includes a kneeling young person handling an incense burner from which smoke rises, and various ornaments and vessels are scattered around. The entire scene is captured in a monochromatic, shaded style typical of graphite or charcoal drawings.

artworks.title: Un léger zéphir annoncant l'arrivée du printemps
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures struggling against the wind. The image depicts strong gusts of wind causing the clothing of the figures to billow dramatically. One figure is on the left, wearing a voluminous dress, while the figure on the right is wearing a heavy coat and holding onto their hat. A hat is seen flying off into the air. The artistic style is reminiscent of 19th-century caricature work, with exaggerated features and expressions.
